name: Extralobar Congenital Pulmonary Sequestration

criteria.description: Presence of non-functioning lung tissue with systemic arterial supply separate from pulmonary arteries
Sequestered lung tissue enclosed within its own pleural covering distinct from normal lung
No communication between sequestered lung tissue and tracheobronchial tree
Identification of systemic arterial supply and pleural encapsulation on imaging (CT/MRI)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anomalous systemic arterial supply, extralobar pleural encapsulation, and absence of bronchial connection confirmed by imaging or histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often confirmed postnatally by imaging and surgical pathology

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systemic arterial supply to non-functioning lung tissue
pathognomonic.notes: Identified via imaging; hallmark of sequestration
searchTerms: abnormal artery supplying non-working lung tissue
extra blood vessel feeding lung segment
systemic artery to lung area without function

pathognomonic.symptomName: Extralobar pleural encapsulation of sequestered lung
pathognomonic.notes: Distinct pleural covering separate from normal lung
searchTerms: lung tissue separated by pleural covering

common.notes: May present with tachypnea or cyanosis
Due to impaired drainage of sequestered tissue
Often detected prenatally or incidentally in infants

common.symptomName: Chest wall deformity or mass effect
common.notes: Due to mass effect of sequestered tissue

searchTerms: heart and vessel problems from blood shunting
cardiovascular issues due to abnormal blood flow

occasional.notes: May occur secondary to inflammation or infection

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as expected

rare.notes: Secondary to chronic hypoxia or shunting

searchTerms: abnormal connection between bronchus and pleura
air leak from lung to chest cavity

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers elevated if infected
Normal routine blood counts unless secondary infection
imaging: CT or MRI showing systemic arterial supply to sequestered lung tissue
Extralobar pleural encapsulation visible on imaging
Absence of bronchial communication on bronchography or CT
genetic: No known genetic mutations directly associated
Considered a congenital malformation without defined genetic etiology
other: Histopathology confirming non-functioning lung tissue with systemic arterial supply
Surgical findings of separate pleural covering

distinguishingFeatures: Intralobar sequestration shares pleural covering with normal lung
Usually presents later in childhood or adulthood
Presence of cystic lung lesions communicating with bronchial tree

references: Stocker JT. Congenital pulmonary airway malformation and pulmonary sequestration. Semin Diagn Pathol. 2010.
Savic B, Birtel FJ, Tholen W, Funke HD, Knoche R. Lung sequestration: report of seven cases and review of 540 published cases. Thorax. 1979.
Corbett HJ, Humphrey GM. Pulmonary sequestration. Paediatr Respir Rev. 2004.
